groups.text: A coroutine scores two million card transactions in a C P U loop.
Java has no coroutines, so this one is Kotlin only.
Halfway through, the service shuts down and calls cancel on the job.
Here is the loop.
Halfway, cancel arrives, and the job's state changes to cancelling.
But the loop does not stop.
It scores every row, to the very end.
That is because cancel doesn't stop anything.
It only marks the job as cancelling.
The coroutine has to notice the mark itself.
Compare a second coroutine, waiting in delay for ten seconds.
It is cancelled at the same moment.
delay is a suspension point, and it checks the mark.
The coroutine is resumed at once with a CancellationException.
The exception unwinds the stack, finally blocks run, and the job ends as cancelled.
withContext, await, join, yield, and a channel's send and receive check the same way.
The scan loop only calls score, a plain function, so it never reaches such a point.
A blocking call, like Thread.sleep or a JDBC query, never reads the mark either.
This is cooperative cancellation.
Cancel is a request, and your code has to notice it.
So a C P U loop checks now and then.
ensureActive throws CancellationException once the job is cancelled.
Cancel at the same point.
The next check, at most a thousand rows later, sees the mark and throws.
finally runs, and the job ends as cancelled.
The loop stopped within a thousand rows of the cancel.
ensureActive is one of three tools.
isActive gives you a Boolean, for a loop that wants to stop quietly.
yield checks too, and also lets other coroutines on the same dispatcher run.
A check is only a read of the job's state, so it costs almost nothing.
Once every few hundred rows is plenty.
